fact: 1930年7月26日，瓦加斯在总统选举中的竞选搭档若昂·佩索阿（João Pessoa）在累西腓被若昂·丹塔斯刺杀，动机兼有政治与私人恩怨。此案成为武装动员的导火索，帕拉伊巴州首府随即陷入混乱。此前1929年，现任总统华盛顿·路易斯指定圣保罗人儒利奥·普雷斯特斯为继任者，打破米纳斯吉拉斯与圣保罗轮流执政的「咖啡加牛奶」惯例，米纳斯吉拉斯、南里奥格兰德与帕拉伊巴遂组成自由联盟支持瓦加斯；自由联盟拒绝承认选举结果，指普雷斯特斯靠舞弊获胜，而实际上双方都操纵了选民。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Brazilian Revolution of 1930
sources.quote: On July 26, 1930, João Pessoa, Vargas's running mate in the 1930 election, was assassinated by João Dantas in Recife for political and personal reasons. ... The Liberal Alliance refused to accept the validity of the elections and claiming that Prestes' victory had been due to fraud. In reality, both sides had manipulated the electorate. ... the presidency had alternated between them every election until 1929, when incumbent President Washington Luís declared his successor would be Júlio Prestes, also from São Paulo.

fact: 1930年10月3日下午5时30分，南里奥格兰德州在瓦加斯与戈伊斯·蒙泰罗领导下起事；当晚10时革命者攻占阿雷格里港，击败阿尔梅达及其部众，代价是20人死亡。至10月10日，革命者已控制整个南里奥格兰德州；次日北方与东北部在茹阿雷斯·塔沃拉领导下响应，米纳斯吉拉斯在一周内正式倒向革命一方。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Brazilian Revolution of 1930
sources.quote: Vargas, now in charge of picking a date, decided to begin instead at 5:30 p.m. on October 3 in Rio Grande do Sul. ... at 10:00 p.m. on October 3, the revolutionaries had claimed the city of Porto Alegre and had defeated Almeida and his gaucho troops, at a cost of 20 people dead. ... the revolutionaries had controlled the entire state by October 10.

fact: 1930年10月24日晨，担心长期内战的军官自行发动军事政变，推翻华盛顿·路易斯，成立三人「安抚执政委员会」；总统被告知可依靠2600名士兵，但守卫瓜纳巴拉宫的警察旅选择不抵抗。11月3日，执政委员会把权力交给瓦加斯，开启长达15年的瓦加斯时代；11月11日瓦加斯颁布法令授予自己独裁权力。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Brazilian Revolution of 1930
sources.quote: Military officers, acting independently of both the government and the revolutionaries, worried about the possibility of a protracted civil war, swiftly led a military coup to depose Luís in Rio de Janeiro, on 24 October. ... the junta gave up power to Vargas on 3 November, a month after the revolution had broken out, which started a fifteen-year-long presidency. ... on 11 November, he issued a decree granting himself dictatorial powers.

fact: 20世纪初咖啡占巴西国民生产总值的16%、出口收入的四分之三；1920年代巴西供应世界咖啡的80%。1929年华尔街崩盘后经济动荡，咖啡价格急剧下跌，而此前数十年的「咖啡保卫」（valorization）政策——政府收购过剩收成、待价而沽——虽在种植者与政府看来是成功的，却造成全球性过剩，并在1930年代大萧条中放大了损失。这意味着1930年圣保罗的危机不是单纯的价格下跌，而是「长期托市造成的库存」与「外部需求崩塌」的叠加。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Coffee production in Brazil
sources.quote: By the early 20th century, coffee accounted for 16% of Brazil's gross national product, and three-fourths of its export earnings. ... In the 1920s, Brazil had a near monopoly of the international coffee market, supplying 80% of the world's coffee. ... The valorization scheme was successful from the perspective of the planters and the Brazilian state, but led to a global oversupply and increased the damages from the crash during the Great Depression in the 1930s.

fact: 瓦加斯政府上台时的财政状况，可由奥斯瓦尔多·阿拉尼亚的描述概括：「国家没有钱，没有外汇，事实上与法律上都处于延期偿付状态，数日内到期或即将到期的对外承诺无法履行；联邦、州与地方三级浮动债务从未被计算过；咖啡处于三重危机——价格、生产过剩、仓库里的大量存货；巴西的经济、工业与劳工一片废墟；还有一场失业危机。」这段描述是1930年11月政权交接时对新政府处境的同期判断。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Brazilian Revolution of 1930，Causes – Economic crisis
sources.quote: The country was without money, without exchange, actually and legally in a moratorium with pressing promises to be met abroad, due or to become due in a few days; a floating debt, federal, state, and local, which had never been calculated; coffee in three crises—prices, overproduction, and large stocks in warehouses; Brazilian economy, industry, and labor in ruin; and an unemployment crisis.

fact: 1930年11月11日，瓦加斯颁布法令授予自己独裁权力，以「临时政府」形式统治，旧共和国（1889—1930）的宪政秩序随之中断；新宪法要到1934年才颁布。对居住者而言，这意味着1930年11月之后财产权、合同与行政命令的效力来源从议会转为临时总统的法令，规则的稳定性取决于个人权威而非制度。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Brazilian Revolution of 1930
sources.quote: About a week later, on 11 November, he issued a decree granting himself dictatorial powers.

fact: 巴西的咖啡保卫政策（valorization）自20世纪初开始实施：政府买下过剩收成、在国际市场择机出售，以稳定价格。1906年2月《陶巴特协定》是两个最大产州（里约热内卢与米纳斯吉拉斯）为限产限出口、操纵价格而签署的典型安排，短期抬高了价格并刺激了继续扩产。该政策在种植者与政府看来是成功的，却造成全球过剩，并在1930年代大萧条中放大损失。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Coffee production in Brazil
sources.quote: The February 1906 Taubaté Agreement is a clear example of the large political influence São Paulo wielded owing to its role in the coffee trade. Overproduction had decreased the price of coffee, and to protect the coffee industry ... the government was to control the price by buying abundant harvests and selling the beans on the international market at a better opportunity. The scheme sparked a temporary rise in the price and promoted the continued expansion of coffee production.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Brazilian Revolution of 1930
sources.quote: in 1906, the two largest coffee-producing states, Rio de Janeiro and Minas, signed an agreement to limit exports and production to manipulate the price of coffee. The attempt to raise the price of coffee failed but prevented it from declining even further.

fact: 圣保罗的工业基础是在咖啡贸易之上建立起来的：意大利移民、1888年废奴以及咖啡种植者与奶农之间「咖啡加牛奶」的政治联盟，共同支撑了圣保罗的工业化与共和国政治，直至1930年。1930年革命终结了圣保罗与米纳斯吉拉斯轮流执政的格局，圣保罗的政治影响力随之下降，但其工业与港口（桑托斯港）仍是全国经济的核心。

sources.title: Uniflection, Chapter 10 Imperialism, Colonial Economies, and the Global Periphery
sources.quote: Brazilian coffee built São Paulo's industrial base through Italian immigration, abolition in 1888, and the política café com leite alliance between coffee planters and dairy ranchers that dominated republican politics through 1930.
